CONFIDENCE: 0.23
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is typical of a simple aliphatic poly-ether with many CH2 groups and no strong hetero-atom multiple bonds.  
• Very intense band at 836 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the symmetric C-O-C stretch of an ether; this is the strongest Raman line of ethylene-oxide/ethylene-glycol derivatives and matches diethylene glycol (candidate 2).  
• Medium bands at 1015, 1112–1130 and 1218 cm⁻¹ correspond to C-O and C-C stretching modes seen in glycol spectra, while 1306 cm⁻¹ (CH2 wag) and 1446 cm⁻¹ (CH2 scissor) agree with a chain of CH2 groups.  
• The C-H stretching envelope with peaks at 2862, 2895 and 2972 cm⁻¹ fits an all-aliphatic molecule.  
• No peak appears in the 2200–2300 cm⁻¹ region, excluding the isocyanate (candidate 3) and other multiple-bonded species; other candidates lacking an ether group cannot explain the dominant 836 cm⁻¹ line.  

Therefore the best match is diethylene glycol, SMILES CCOCCO (candidate 2).
